## What travels through Git

Project identity, repository URLs and default branches, relationships, the member roster with each member's band and roles, product pins and the launcher, role defaults, per-member ID files, records, and durable knowledge are shared. Roles say what a member contributes and authorize nothing.

## What stays on the machine

Checkout paths, active member, base branches, local role overrides, worktree associations, installed dependencies, and environment files are local. So is `.claude/settings.local.json`, where `agent setup` adds Claude Code's `attribution` setting to turn commit and pull request attribution off; it is gitignored, so every machine runs `agent setup` to receive it. A second machine connects its own copies; it does not reinitialize the shared workspace.

Trust in extension scripts is local too. `extensions.yaml` says which extensions the workspace uses and is shared, but whether an extension's scripts may run is recorded per member and per machine in the ignored `.context-circuit/local/extension-trust.yaml`, written only by `extension allow` at the person's request. A clone carries no allows: each member allows each version on each machine they work on, after reading what its scripts do. Fetched remote extensions under `.context-circuit/local/extensions/` stay on the machine as well.

A local `base_branch` can differ from the remote's shared `default_branch`. Worktree starting points and delivery targets must read the local binding.

## Join safely

Select an existing member, run `workspace connect`, obtain or connect each repository, and run `agent setup`. Use separate compatible checkouts and runtime dependencies for native Windows, WSL, remote hosts, and containers. Shared Git history does not move uncommitted work or installed tools.
